title: Configure and manage starter pools in Fabric Spark - Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Starter pools cut Spark session startup by drawing on pre-warmed capacity, but Microsoft documents them as a best-effort, Microsoft-managed optimization: pre-warmed capacity is not guaranteed for a given run, and when none is available Fabric falls back to standard on-demand capacity and the session takes correspondingly longer.

For workloads that need a predictable session start — scheduled Spark job definitions and other latency-sensitive jobs — Microsoft's documented answer is a custom live pool, which keeps dedicated clusters warm during an active window you control and starts sessions in approximately 5 seconds, with environment libraries preinstalled on the hydrated cluster.
Starter pools always use Medium nodes; autoscale and dynamic executor allocation are both enabled by default and can be adjusted, but the node size itself is not a starter-pool setting.

Fabric capacity SKUs map to Spark vCores at two vCores per capacity unit — F2 gives 4, F8 gives 16, F64 gives 128, F256 gives 512 — and each SKU caps starter pool size: F2 and F4 permit a single node, F64 defaults to 10 nodes with a maximum of 16, and F512 and above default to 10 with maxima of 128 to 200 nodes.
Customizing a workspace's starter pool requires the workspace Admin role, and the settings live under Workspace settings → Data Engineering/Science → Spark settings.
